outcome: Srihari can now ask the 3F Financial MIS questions in plain English and get answers he can check. The assistant is registered and governed: every question runs through the same authorization, semantic layer and SQL guard as the reports, so an answer is either the governed numbers with a verified badge and its provenance - the readback, the measures, the scope and the data-as-of behind a disclosure - or an honest refusal that says why. It declines what it must not answer: a causal 'why is labour high' is refused rather than guessed at, a question outside the registered catalog returns not-supported rather than a plausible number, and a greeting is answered deterministically without ever reaching the model. Answers are asked and read in two places, the panel docked beside the MIS report and a standalone Ask page, and 'view in report' opens the statement the answer came from, or says plainly why it cannot. He can save a question and pin it to his dashboard, then reopen either from Explore or the dashboard - and reopening RE-RUNS the saved selection against current data rather than replaying a stored answer, because nothing at rest holds one: the vendored snapshot machinery was deleted outright. Every reopen re-authorizes as the current user against the current semantic layer, so a selection he may no longer run comes back as a refusal that says so rather than a stale figure or a silently missing row, and it stays visible and deletable. The model runs on Bedrock in ap-south-1, and the boundary is enforced by test on the provider's own arguments: his question, the prior turns and the governed vocabulary may leave the app; amounts, measure values, transaction lines and result rows never do.
title: Assistant + exploration
